back: Spending on buying, bringing into use or improving non-current assets; benefits more than one year.
Spending on running the business and maintaining assets; benefits the current year only.

front: Costs included in the cost of a non-current asset
back: Purchase price, delivery, installation, testing, legal fees: everything needed to get it ready for use.
Improvement (extension, upgrade, longer life) = capital. Repair or maintenance (restore existing condition) = revenue.
Statement of financial position, as a non-current asset (then depreciated).
Income statement (statement of profit or loss), as an expense or in cost of sales.
Money received that is not normal trading income: loans, capital introduced, proceeds from selling non-current assets.
Income from normal activities: sales, rent received, commission received, interest received.

front: Wages paid to install a machine
back: Capital expenditure: part of the machine's cost.
